framework/modelcatalog/sync.go:129-141 and :513-525 (one-shot ValidateExternalURL then bare http.Client)
transports/bifrost-http/handlers/config.go:989-1008 (one-shot ValidateExternalURL then bare client.Get, redirects followed)

routes: T1/T2: request-supplied resource fetch to reserved shared range, broadcast, site-local and 6to4/NAT64-wrapped internal IPv4; public targets in the same transition forms stay fetchable
T3: provider dial guard for 6to4/NAT64-wrapped internal IPv4 and site-local; loopback always reachable, RFC 1918 reachable under the opt-in, proxy dial preserved
T6/T7: configured pricing and model-parameters endpoints, direct and via a redirect from a local endpoint; file://, loopback and RFC 1918 endpoints keep working
T8: admin reachability check, direct and via a redirect; local, private-LAN and file endpoints keep working
T9: upstream-supplied image URL; inline base64 and ordinary public targets keep working

local.project: the selected dialer and reachability tests pass on the pinned tree; the full suites need network and a database

traps.shape: the request-fetch address deny-list treats the reserved shared range, the broadcast address, the deprecated site-local range and an IPv4 carried inside 6to4 / NAT64 (well-known and local-use with the RFC 6052 u-octet skipped) as public
traps.realistic_because: the published advisory's own route; the deny-list is real upstream code at the pinned commit

traps.shape: the coupled must-keep-working value next to the transition-form hole: a public IPv4 carried in 6to4 or NAT64 must stay fetchable, so the repair has to unwrap and re-check rather than block the prefix
traps.realistic_because: real upstream code; the over-broad prefix block is the repair a careful engineer is most likely to write

traps.shape: the shared private-address classifier used by the provider dial guard does not unwrap IPv6 transition forms and does not cover the deprecated site-local range, while it must keep loopback always reachable and RFC 1918 reachable under the operator opt-in
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: a generic address helper with its own callers, not the SSRF check the advisory names

traps.shape: the configured pricing download validates the URL once with the private-network opt-in and then uses a bare client; a transition-written literal and a redirect target are never checked
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; operator-supplied configuration is a plausible reason to treat the save-time check as sufficient

traps.shape: the configured model-parameters download has the same one-shot validation and bare client as the pricing download, one feature away in the same file
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the neighbouring feature is easy to overlook once the first loader is repaired

traps.shape: the admin reachability check validates once with the private-network opt-in and then follows redirects with a bare client, so a redirect lands on an unchecked destination
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; performing the reachability request is the point of the feature, which is a strong reason to read the missing check as intended

traps.shape: the response-to-image converter downloads an upstream-supplied image URL with a fasthttp client that has no address check at all; the same guarded operation is implemented a second time, independently of the request fetch guard
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the URL comes from the upstream provider's response, a clean reason to dismiss it as not attacker-controlled

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the task has no per-resource authorisation; the protected thing is the destination address
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: no roles, peers or request directions exist on this surface
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every protected operation is an outbound connection; there is no read/write variant
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no normalising or adjusting step runs between the supplied address and the check
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no role or secret authority is consulted on any of these paths

advisories.rule: the pinned commit is the parent of the published fix

history.policy: the published fix covers the request-resource fetch guard (concept T1/T2) only; the other four concepts are unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit, so applying the published fix alone leaves them open
